content.text:
Finding submitted. Summary of the review:

**Status: deviation (high severity) — Section 4.2(a), Termination Payment**

**What the document does**
- **§4.1** — one-year term, auto-renewing annually, terminable by *either* Party on 90 days' written notice.
- **§4.2(a)** — if *the Company* terminates, we owe HDI a Termination Payment of (trailing 12-month Net Sales − $800,000) ÷ 2.
- **§4.2(b)** — expressly one-way: HDI never owes us a reciprocal payment.

**What passes**
The notice mechanics sit at the playbook fallback and I did not redline them: our 90-day exit is within the 60–90 day band, and HDI's convenience right is on 90 days' notice — not *fewer* than 90, so it stays out of walk-away territory. The 90-day (vs. preferred 30-day) notice and the absent pro-rata refund mechanic are noted in the rationale only; the refund point has little bite here since fees are paid monthly in arrears under §3.2, not prepaid.

**What fails**
The exit fee breaks the fallback cap of "3 months' fees." Our fees are 30% of monthly Net Sales above $11,000, so at ~$2M annual Net Sales the formula produces roughly $600,000 against roughly $140,000 of three months' fees — and it scales without limit as the Site succeeds. It also triggers on *any* Company termination, including termination for HDI's own breach, which would quietly override the without-penalty right we already hold in §1.6.

**Redline approach**
I deliberately pitched at the fallback rather than the preferred 30-day/no-penalty position. HDI bears all design, development, hosting and maintenance cost under §§1.2–1.3 and is paid solely through revenue share, so some recovery on an early exit is the actual bargain — demanding a penalty-free walk would be disproportionate. The edit caps the payment at three months' §3.1 fees and carves out terminations under §1.6 or for HDI's breach, leaving the rest of the clause intact.

One item worth flagging for the deal team, outside this rule's scope: §4.1 is ambiguous as to whether the 90-day notice is a non-renewal notice or a free-standing right to terminate mid-term. Under either reading the notice period clears the fallback, so it did not change this finding, but clarifying it would remove a real dispute risk about when the capped fee is even payable.
